transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together because we have a subpoena response package due to the court this month, and I need to review the current draft before giving my final approval. As part of our standard process, I'll be consulting with both litigation counsel and compliance before we produce anything. The draft currently covers interview materials, investigative analyses, and the identity of the reporting employee. I'd like to walk through each of those components and make sure we're all aligned on what should and shouldn't be included. Who has the latest version of the draft in front of them?

transcript.text: Elena, before we go through the draft component by component, I need to flag something critical I found while reviewing the court docket. There's a stipulated protective order entered on April 3, 2025, that directly governs our production. It requires that factual interview summaries be produced by May 20, 2025, that attorney mental impressions and legal analysis may be withheld, and that a confidentiality designation must accompany the production. The docket alert was routed only to the litigation queue, so I haven't yet added these requirements to the response draft. We need to make sure the draft is updated to comply with this order before you give final approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag something critical from the compliance side. I found a signed request in the compliance intake system from the reporting employee that requires identity-redacted production and exactly 90 days of independent retaliation monitoring. This request was filed in the compliance system rather than the legal-response workspace, so it is not reflected in the current draft. Given that the draft currently includes the reporting employee's identity, we have a direct conflict that needs to be resolved before you give final approval.

That satisfies both the protective order's production mandate and the compliance request's redaction requirement. I'll update the draft to: one, add the confidentiality designation; two, separate factual summaries from legal analysis, withholding the latter; and three, redact the reporting employee's identity throughout.
